processes.description: A logistics lead or manager announces who now handles which pooling points, industrial accounts, counterparties or duties, usually when someone joins, leaves or a desk is realigned. Recipients reply to confirm or to point out pieces that look unassigned, and departing or moving staff confirm what they hand over. Some rounds introduce new staff or share contact extensions so others know whom to call for work moved off another desk.
steps: A staff change, reorganisation or new account triggers a reassignment.
The lead drafts a memo listing each pipeline, point or account and its new owner and backup.
The memo is sent to the desk and forwarded to affected groups.
Recipients check the list against what they handle and flag gaps or items left unassigned.
Outgoing and incoming owners confirm the handover of specific accounts.
A follow-up memo settles the open items and contact details.

stalls.summary: Pieces of work fall through the reassignment: an HPL operational duty is reported as left unassigned, and the follow-up memo still lists it as unresolved.
Handovers of specific accounts are disputed in the mail, with the previous scheduler doubting the new owner could handle an account he believes he now covers.

contradictions.summary: Ownership of the industrial accounts is stated differently: one forward says they transition to Robert as of January 1, Robert says he has taken over all industrial accounts, while the previous scheduler questions whether he can handle Valero yet agrees to leave the accounts to him.
The desk assumed Carlos had taken over a departing colleague's work, while the same message reports an HPL operational duty as unassigned, so who owns that work was unclear.

automation.approach: Keep one shared assignment register listing every pipeline, pooling point, account and duty with its owner and backup. A reassignment memo is generated from the changes to the register, and any item without an owner is flagged before the memo goes out.
automation.rationale: The confusion in the mail comes from items missing from free-text memos. A register laid out by item, owner and backup makes gaps visible and gives the desk one place to check who handles what.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to compiling the list of points and accounts being moved, checking it against current coverage, resolving gaps such as unassigned duties, and updating contact or system records. Most rounds are short announcements; a full desk realignment takes longer. A register could produce the list and flag gaps, while decisions on who takes what stay with people.

processes.description: Shippers and interconnecting parties ask for new transport contracts, amendments, MDQ increases or operational balancing agreements. The marketer or contract administrator checks the request, submits it to CAS for capacity approval, approves it with the contract number, and routes amendments for signature. Draft language is revised between commercial and legal staff before going to the customer, and status reports track contracts outstanding. Open items such as unsigned OBAs or contracts under legal review are chased.
steps: A shipper or internal group requests a contract, amendment, MDQ change or OBA.
The marketer confirms terms with the customer, often by phone.
The request is submitted to CAS for capacity approval.
Contract language is drafted or revised, with legal review where needed.
The approval and contract number are sent back and amendments are routed for signature.
Signed agreements are logged and status reports track what remains outstanding.

stalls.summary: Requests wait on replies and on legal review: a requester reports no updates on an unresolved issue affecting a customer, and another only knows legal was reviewing the contract.
A contract sent for review and initial weeks earlier has its status chased, showing documents stall between hands.
Requests and agreements go round again: a customer revises its own assignment request, and an OBA stays outstanding until the counterparty name is changed.

automation.approach: A contract request form capturing contract number, counterparty, quantities, dates and rates feeds a tracker that records CAS submission, approval, legal review and signature status. The tracker produces the status report and flags items that have waited too long for review or signature.
automation.rationale: Most rounds are structured MDQ or amendment changes, and the stalls are items lost in review. A standard request form plus status tracker cuts retyping of terms and makes outstanding contracts visible without chasing.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to checking the contract and requested quantities, entering the CAS capacity request, approving and recording the change, and for amendments or OBAs drafting or revising language and routing it for signature. Simple MDQ increases are quick; new OBAs with language revisions take longer. Forms and tracking can be automated, but terms and legal language need people.

processes.description: When the methanol or MTBE plant trips, runs at reduced rates or restarts, the plant contact sends a short notice to gas schedulers and commercial staff describing the cause, such as a boiler taken out or a broken compressor shaft, and the expected restart. Updates follow as the restart estimate moves, ending with a notice that the plant is up and making spec product. Schedulers use these notices to adjust the gas they nominate to the plant.
steps: The plant goes down, cuts rates or plans a restart.
The plant contact sends a notice with the cause and expected timing.
Schedulers adjust gas nominations to the plant's expected burn.
Updates are sent as the restart estimate changes.
A final notice confirms the plant is producing spec product.

stalls.summary: Restart timing is often unknown or keeps moving, leaving schedulers waiting on further notices before they can settle volumes.

automation.approach: A standard outage notice form with fields for plant, status, cause, current rate, expected restart and expected gas use, sent to a fixed distribution list, so schedulers get the same facts in the same place each time.
automation.rationale: The notices are short and repetitive. A fixed template ensures each one states the expected gas impact and restart time that schedulers need to rebalance nominations.

work_estimate.rationale: Minutes go to the plant contact confirming status and restart estimates with operations, and to schedulers adjusting nominations for the changed plant load. The notices themselves are brief and the quotes show little beyond them, so the estimate stays small. A template helps the notice, while the operational judgement and nomination changes stay manual.
